title: Fix an instrument misloaded across a sterilization cassette, seat both loose ones, close the lid and hook the latch
instruction: Leave the instrument cassette ready for the sterilizer: all five instruments snapped down, each into a rail slot of its own, lid closed flat and the latch clip hooked, grippers off the cassette.
context: Done by: dental assistants (O*NET 31-9091.00; 388,600 US workers, 2025) and dental hygienists (29-1292.00; 225,300; task 'Maintain dental equipment and sharpen and sterilize dental instruments.'), 613,900 together (BLS employment figures as shown on O*NET OnLine). O*NET lists for dental assistants 'sterilize or disinfect instruments, set up instrument trays'. After each patient the used instruments go back into the cassette's rails and the closed, locked cassette goes to the washer and autoclave. The maker's 2020 cassette catalog (troubleshooting table) names 'overloading / improperly placed instruments' as the cause of broken hinges and says 'only light force is needed to close the cassette'. This trial starts from that error: the explorer lies across the cassette instead of in its slot, holding the lid about 1 cm open. The robot has to find it, lift it out, turn it a quarter turn and snap it past the rail lips into a free slot, load the mirror, then close the lid and lock the clip.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). A stainless 5-instrument exam cassette at real size (7.6 x 20.3 x 3.2 cm closed, maker catalog) sits fixed in a 0.6 cm bench holder centred at (30.0, 0.0), long side toward the robot. Its two blue silicone rails, 12 cm apart, each have five notches at 1.27 cm pitch across the 7.6 cm width; at every notch mouth a sprung silicone lip (round edge, 0.2 cm across) sticks 0.25 cm into the 1.05 cm mouth and narrows it to 0.8 cm, so a 0.95 cm handle rests on the lips until it is pressed past them (one lip per rail, on the notch's +x side; to pass, a handle pushes it back about 0.13-0.15 cm by the geometry, about 3 N/mm, an estimate) and is then held under them. The lid, hinged on the back long edge (+x), leans open at 120 degrees; a blue press pad under it clears a seated handle by 0.8 mm. The red latch clip (2.3 x 1.2 cm, pivot on the lid's front top edge) leans back over the lid, open; swung forward and down it hangs over the front, its hook tab under a steel keeper lip (0.12 x 2.4 x 0.12 cm) on the base's front wall. Three loose instruments (stainless, 16.5 cm long, 13 cm round handle 0.95 cm thick) are snapped into slots 1, 3 and 5, held only by the rail lips; slots 2 and 4 are free. Misload: an explorer (20 g) lies across the cassette, handle along x, centre (27.0, 4.7), resting on the front rim and over the seated instruments, so the lid cannot close. A mouth mirror (20 g) lies on a white resin tray (6.4 x 19 x 0.6 cm, centre (22.2, 0.0), a 0.4 cm lip on its back edge and low cradle ridges near the handle ends so a handle cannot roll) in front of the cassette, in its cradle at about (23.4-24.0, 0.0) (it settles against the cradle ridge at 23.4), handle along y. The bench holder is a black anodised plate 10 x 22.7 x 0.6 cm with corner stops.
scoring: Read from the final state with simple tools, after the run ends: photo of the final scene; 1 mm feeler gauge at the lid's front edge; then the scorer opens the lid and checks each handle by eye and ruler (seated = down in both rail notches, below its lip tops, one instrument per slot); latch = clip hanging down over the front with its hook tab caught under the keeper lip, by eye (simulator: the tab's top edge under the lip, overlapping it by 0.5 mm or more and no more than 2 mm below it, clip at least 88 degrees down); grippers off = both grippers clear of the cassette and tray in the final photo. An instrument counts as seated when its handle lies along its slot, snapped down in both rail notches (centre within 3 mm of the slot line, within 8 mm of the middle along the slot so both handle ends lie at least 1 mm on their rails, and no more than 1 mm above its seated height, which is only reached past the rail lips); two in one slot count once. 0.2 for each of the two loose instruments (the explorer and the mirror) seated in a free slot (0.4). +0.3: lid closed flat, front gap 1 mm or less. +0.3: latch clip swung down over the front with its hook tab under the keeper lip (as above), on a flat lid, with both grippers off: each gripper's tool-centre point outside the box made of the cassette and tray (x 19.0 to 35.8, y -10.2 to +10.2) grown by 5 cm on every side, up to 14.9 cm above the bench. Lid and latch points count only if all five instruments are seated. Possible: 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.7, 1.0.
reset_notes: Swing the clip up and back over the lid, open the lid to its 120-degree stop, pull instruments 2 and 4 out past the rail lips, lay the mirror in its tray cradle at about (23.4-24.0, 0.0) and lay the explorer across the cassette, handle along x, centre (27.0, 4.7), on the front rim.
fidelity: Cassette size and layout 1:1 from the maker's catalog. Estimates: handle size, notch pitch, rail spacing, pad height, clip size, and the rail lips' size and spring (one sprung lip per rail at every notch); a rebuild should match the 0.8 cm lipped mouth and about 3 N/mm per lip. All five instruments are loose; the rail lips hold the seated ones. The cassette sits in a bench holder. The over-centre clip hooks a separate keeper lip: a 2 N lid pull lifts the lid 0.76 deg hooked, 10 deg unhooked.
